clinicalPearls: Deficiency of biotin (a B-group vitamin and enzyme cofactor) causes a characteristic dermatitis, alopecia and neurological features
The classic cutaneous sign is a periorificial scaly erythematous dermatitis with hair loss
Neurological features include lethargy, hypotonia, paraesthesiae and, in infants, developmental effects
Acquired causes include prolonged consumption of raw egg white (avidin binds biotin), long-term parenteral nutrition without biotin, and some anticonvulsants
Inherited biotinidase deficiency and holocarboxylase synthetase deficiency are important congenital causes detected on newborn screening
It responds rapidly to biotin replacement
reference.pathophysiology: Biotin is a cofactor for carboxylase enzymes central to gluconeogenesis, fatty acid synthesis and amino acid metabolism. Deficiency impairs these carboxylases, disturbing energy and lipid metabolism in the skin, hair follicles and nervous system and producing the dermatitis, alopecia and neurological features. Acquired deficiency follows reduced intake or absorption or increased binding (avidin in raw egg white), while inherited biotinidase or holocarboxylase synthetase deficiency prevents recycling or utilisation of biotin, causing an organic aciduria if untreated.
additionalDifferentials: Other nutritional dermatitides (essential fatty acid, niacin)
additionalInvestigations: Clinical recognition of the dermatitis-alopecia-neurological pattern
Biotinidase activity and, in infants, newborn screening results
Assessment of diet, parenteral nutrition and medications
Urinary organic acids where an inherited disorder is suspected
redFlags: Infant with dermatitis, seizures and metabolic acidosis (possible biotinidase deficiency)
reference.prognosis: Acquired deficiency and inherited biotinidase deficiency respond well and often completely to biotin, particularly when inherited disease is treated early after newborn screening.
pitfalls: Missing biotinidase deficiency, which is treatable and screened for in newborns
Overlooking dietary raw egg white or biotin-free parenteral nutrition
Confusing it with zinc deficiency dermatitis
Delaying treatment in an unwell infant
